citation_verdicts.note: Supports steward accountability, but only for Reference Data; the same bullet does not extend to Master Data (A-03 position wording is consistent with this).
Same bullet adds that a system of reference may be needed for sharing; does not limit the quoted claim.

Page and wording are accurate, but the passage is a storage technique for Reference Data (synonym rings for search), not term synonyms in a business glossary. It supports the reader's stated caveat, not any glossary-synonym claim for A-10.
Reconciliation here means consolidating sources into a master record; reader's caveat on A-25 about the different project meaning of 'reconciliation' is correct.
Text says 'This could include', so it is a suggestion, which matches the reader's 'suggests'. Table 23 is missing, as the reader notes.
Sentence continues from the page 626 label; context supports steward-coverage metric identifying gaps in support.

row_verdicts.note: Partial/wording is fair. Decision rights match Ch10 (accountability decisions left to people and governance bodies). Project does define Project Owner and Data Steward in GOVERNANCE-DECISIONS.md but never defines Data Owner or 'ownership gap'; the contract does have an ownership_gaps output field, which the reader acknowledges.

Aligned/citation is defensible: project behaviour (surface conflicts, escalate to a human steward) is consistent with Ch10 on reconciling names and definitions. Grade is thin because Ch10 never treats a business glossary and uses 'synonym' only for search synonym rings; the reader flags this as provisional. Recommend dropping C10-09 as a supporting citation and leaning on C10-12, C10-23, C10-24, C10-27.

Missing/structural-proposal is fair. My search of the repo markdown and contracts found no reference or master data stewardship artefact; 'reconciliation' appears once as a Context-agent content area. Note option 3 (Context-agent scope only) is a weak option that leaves the gap open, as the reader admits; record-deviation remains an available alternative.

Partial/wording is fair. Project names authoritative sources per agent and ranks internal documented position first (a control DMBOK2 does not address); it has no system of record versus system of reference distinction for data. Reader says no counterpart exists, but docs/IMPLEMENTATION-SEQUENCE.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE-RISKS.md do use 'system of record' for case-state storage, which is a different sense and does not change the grade.

missing_findings.note: Section 2.2.2 says owners of existing reference data must understand the benefits of central management and agree to support stewardship; directly relevant to ownership assignment and not cited.

Data acquisition bullet 'Determining who will be responsible for monitoring and maintaining the quality of a new source's data' (starts at end of p.598/top p.599) is a further accountability-assignment statement; not cited.

Section 2.2.6 says governance policies should mandate use of reference data from the central repository or a system of reference populated from it; relevant to authoritative-source designation and not cited.
